Apologies for the noise this flaky test has caused upstream. The failure in 13-dataset-actions.spec.ts only surfaces in GitHub Actions. Locally the timing and hardware is forgiving enough that it passes consistently, which made it hard to catch and diagnose earlier.

The root cause seems to be a race condition: after saving metadata, the PrimeFaces DataTable AJAX cycle hadn't fully settled before we were interacting with the select-all checkbox. I've merged a PR with a fix that waits for network idle before the interaction and targets the correct inner PrimeFaces element. Should be stable going forward.

@Ash Manda thanks a ton for these tests . While I was waiting for the API tests to complete, the JSF test failures already uncovered a problem in my latest PR. I was able to unravel the root cause from digging into the report and the logs. This is a huge step forward!

Let me be bold and suggest some improvements: it would be even much better if these tests would...

  1. ... be part of the regular chain (unit, integration, API + JSF).

    • The container images are built three times now: as part of the normal Maven chain, as part of the API tests and as part of the JSF tests. The compute time may be better spent only doing this once. (It takes about 32 minutes to see results)
    • By instrumenting the backend code, we could add more test coverage to the reports which also get sent to SonarCloud. We can save the instrumented code in container images at GHCR, so no re-instrumentation is necessary.
    • We should probably also figure out a better "overarching" test infrastructure where things are easier to understand what trigger which other tests, what relies on what etc. Things are quite all over the place at the moment, which causes some of the redundancies to appear.

  2. ... be easier to correlate. A failing frontend test and what may have gone wrong in the backend need to be put together manually. I understand this is a deep deep rabbit hole, but maybe it's worth looking into options how to make OpenTelemetry spans from Playwright propagate to the backend so we have end-to-end snapshots?

  3. ... have a nicer web UI access for their reports. Downloading the Playwright reports is slooooow and the ZIP is largeish. (1MB/s throughput, 118MB zipfile). Can we upload these HTML reports somewhere else?

    • Also, the traces in the report require looking at these things via http:// or https//, probably due to Javascript & Browser security issues. Opening them locally via file:// denies access to them.
    • I'm aware that OpenTelemetry is probably going to influence these things.

Hi Oliver. Thank you so much for the suggestions! I have thought about all of these things at one point or another, and all of them are on my roadmap. My biggest worry with having the image be built exactly once and having the three tests run in line is state pollution. I was wondering if you had any thoughts on that?

That and if say an API test fails, we probably don't want it to block the pipeline and still have it run the JSF tests anyways. So I felt in the beginning it made a lot more sense to run them separately.

There's probably a way I can get the unit, integration, and JSF tests all run in parallel and produce the reports at the same time. Let me stew on this a bit.

My main point about an "overarching thing" was that once all these tests are done, we need to collate the different reports, merge them (in case of coverage) and do some more things like SonarCloud Analysis, etc
Github action's jobs are meant to be run in parallel. I'm already doing this in some of the existing pipelines.
I am not sure where we could upload the Playwright reports though. S3 maybe? But you pointed out the issue, these reports can't be statically served
so maybe some kind of lambda?
Jobs are only ever run sequentially once you define dependencies between them. Of course a jobs step are always sequential.

Ash Manda said:

results from first tests being included while running the last tests. Like you know not depending on what happens in previous tests, if that makes sense. We faced some issues with this before I believe in the API tests where the count in one of the tests would go off. But these tests would still run within their own realm, right? I agree that we must take care of running each test in a clean environment. With the setup as is I don't see much danger to we'd be able to fall into that trap though. (Ephemeral, separated deployment using compose). This might change if we ever think about moving to use JUnit+Testcontainers to control our pipeline. But we're not there (yet)...?!
Even if we run the jobs in parallel, I was under the assumption that GitHub would reuse the same build.

Ash Manda said:

How does Sonar ingest its coverage metrics? Like how can I help use these test reports ingest into Sonar?

The sonarcloud job is defined here: https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/.github/workflows/maven_unit_test.yml#L184-L220

It consumes the JaCoCo reports we put in place by downloading the artifacts from previous jobs. We configure the location in the POM.

Ash Manda said:

Even if we run the jobs in parallel, I was under the assumption that GitHub would reuse the same build.

No, that is not possible. Each job (which can be parallelized) runs in an ephemeral container, thus must either rebuild or download artifacts. This is very different to what you get from GitLab CI or Jenkins by default (depening on setup/flavor/runner type).

Hello. Good afternoon. A merge commit was made into gdcc/dataverse-jsf-tests to introduce the new expanded test suite going from about ~40 tests across three browsers to about ~80 tests across three browsers.

  1. Improved and stabilized runtimes. Despite the addition of these tests, the full runtime of the tests remains at 30 mins across three browsers. Timeouts and executions were tuned to reduce execution time by about 50%
  2. Reduced artifact size from ~1GiB per successful run to about ~200KiB per successful run
  3. Regression tests for known bugs that can be slowly re-enabled as fixes started to roll in
  4. Basic tests for the brand new locally FAIR features

Please let me know if you start noticing any new failures in the mainstream repo

The test development is now going to enter a freeze. Future updates anticipated:

  1. More regression tests for core code paths
  2. The Container Integration Tests and JSF tests will be rolled into one single re-usable workflow that is capable of running the unit tests, api tests, and frontend tests all at the same time in parallel.
  3. Locally FAIR will be enabled during build time enabling the testing of cutting edge features
I passed this along in Slack.

Just a gentle note for the team. The JSF tests are still in a very very early age of development, they're running in shadow mode right now, basically I'm trying to collect as much data as I can possible to stabilize them, please do not consider the failure of these tests a blocker for merging, for now at this stage, they're an early guide.
